options.C: Morbidity affects only infants while mortality affects mothers
options.D: Morbidity is always preventable while mortality is inevitable

explanation: Think of it this way: morbidity means being sick or having health complications, while mortality simply means death. Simple and clear!

question: What is considered the first and most fundamental function of nursing management?

options.A: Controlling
options.B: Planning
options.C: Directing
options.D: Staffing

explanation: Planning comes first because it sets the direction and goals before any other management function can take place. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h1)

question: What is the most important infection control habit for a nurse to teach a patient on immunosuppressive drugs?

options.A: Stopping all physical exercise completely
options.B: Wearing heavy winter clothing outside at all times
options.C: Drinking only distilled water
options.D: Doing thorough and frequent hand hygiene

explanation: Never underestimate the power of clean hands! Proper hand hygiene is your patient's number one defense against picking up harmful germs in everyday life.

question: Which mineral helps a new mother beat fatigue and rebuild iron stores lost during childbirth?

options.A: Sodium
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Potassium
options.D: Iron

explanation: Iron builds hemoglobin, helping mums recover from delivery blood loss and keeping postpartum fatigue and anemia at bay. You've got this!

question: What is your main duty as a nurse when a patient comes in with complications from an illegal abortion?

options.A: Report her to security before starting any fluids
options.B: Lecture her on the morality of her actions
options.C: Provide immediate, non-judgmental life-saving emergency care
options.D: Refuse treatment until the police arrive

explanation: As a professional nurse, saving a life always comes first. We treat every patient with care, empathy, and zero judgment.

question: Why might an elderly patient with a severe bacterial infection not run a high fever?

options.A: Older adults naturally maintain a much higher internal baseline temperature
options.B: The aging immune system has a blunted inflammatory and febrile response
options.C: Lung tissue infections never trigger body temperature changes at any age
options.D: Circulating white blood cells destroy all heat-producing chemicals instantly

explanation: Brilliant! Because of immunosenescence, older bodies often fail to mount a classic high fever, even when fighting a dangerous infection.

question: Aside from giving fluids, what type of medication is routinely given right away if an infected (septic) abortion is suspected?

options.A: Long-acting oral hypoglycemic agents
options.B: Broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics
options.C: Topical corticosteroid ointments
options.D: Inhaled short-acting beta-agonists

explanation: Infection spreads fast! Starting broad-spectrum IV antibiotics early stops bacteria in their tracks and prevents the patient from sliding into full septic shock.

question: Why do uric acid crystals cause such sudden, sharp pain in a joint?

options.A: White blood cells attack the crystals and release powerful inflammatory chemicals
options.B: The crystals physically cut the main nerve endings inside the joint capsule
options.C: Blood flow to the joint completely stops due to vessel blockage
options.D: Cartilage cells multiply so fast they stretch the joint to its breaking point

explanation: Think of white blood cells rushing in like an emergency crew to clear out the crystals—their cleanup effort triggers a massive wave of swelling and pain!

question: What is the most common and trusted way to sterilize metal surgical tools?

options.A: Boiling in water for twenty minutes
options.B: Steam under pressure in an autoclave
options.C: Ultraviolet radiation in a glass cabinet
options.D: Immersion in liquid bleach solution

explanation: The autoclave is the workhorse of the CSSD! Using high-pressure steam is fast, affordable, and extremely reliable for metal instruments.

question: Why do people with the same genetic background sometimes have different cancer risks?

options.A: Genetics is the only factor that ever influences disease
options.B: Inherited genes change completely every five years
options.C: Their environmental exposures and lifestyle choices vary
options.D: Lifestyle habits have no real impact on cellular health

explanation: Environmental and lifestyle factors interact with genes, meaning different habits will alter overall risk even among family members. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of using qualitative tools in a community assessment?

options.A: To capture local attitudes, cultural beliefs, and human stories
options.B: To measure precise blood pressure and body temperature
options.C: To calculate exact mathematical disease prevalence rates
options.D: To count the total number of hospital beds in the district

explanation: Brilliant! Qualitative methods help you understand the 'why' behind people's behaviors rather than just raw numbers.

question: What is a key nursing duty when caring for a patient with a metabolic disorder?

options.A: Encouraging the patient to eat unlimited amounts of simple sugars
options.B: Prescribing new metabolic medications to cure the underlying defect
options.C: Replacing all oral nutrition with intravenous fluids permanently
options.D: Monitoring laboratory results and tracking dietary intake closely

explanation: As a nurse, keeping a close eye on lab trends and meals helps you catch sneaky metabolic imbalances before they become emergencies!

question: What actually is 'cor pulmonale'?

options.A: Bleeding into the chest cavity following trauma
options.B: An infection of the lining surrounding the lungs
options.C: Right-sided heart failure caused by long-term lung disease
options.D: A sudden collapse of a lung lobe due to a blocked airway

explanation: You nailed it. Long-term lung trouble makes the heart work extra hard on the right side, eventually leading to right-sided heart failure.

question: What is the primary goal of keeping a strict fluid chart on a surgical ward?

options.A: Preventing the patient from needing IV access
options.B: Proving the patient is drinking enough plain water
options.C: Calculating the exact daily hospital food costs
options.D: Detecting early signs of fluid overload or dehydration

explanation: Careful tracking lets nurses spot dangerous imbalances before they cause severe harm. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h2)

question: You notice your clinic frequently runs out of single-use syringes, causing staff to reuse equipment. What is your best professional action?

options.A: Keep quiet so you don't upset the clinic manager during a busy shift
options.B: Buy plastic syringes from a local pharmacy using your own money
options.C: Stop giving all prescribed medications until the hospital closes
options.D: Report the shortage through official channels and advocate for safer supplies

explanation: Spot on! As a nurse, you have a duty to advocate for your patients and push for proper resources when safety is on the line. Great clinical leadership! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h9)

question: A newly widowed patient comes to the clinic looking very weak, dehydrated, and depressed after weeks of isolation. What should be the nurse's first step?

options.A: Advise her to return home and obey the cultural rules quietly
options.B: Report her in-laws immediately to the local village chief for trial
options.C: Stabilize her physical health by addressing dehydration and infections
options.D: Ask her to pay for her hospital registration card before treatment

explanation: Spot on! Emergency nursing always puts life-threatening physical issues—like severe dehydration or infection—first before anything else.

question: Why do we place a waterproof sheet on an operation (surgical) bed?

options.A: To protect the mattress from bodily fluids, blood, and drainage
options.B: To anchor the top blankets securely to the bed frame
options.C: To keep the patient cool during high fever episodes
options.D: To provide extra cushioning for bony prominences

explanation: Spot on! Patients coming from theatre might bleed or vomit, so a waterproof sheet keeps the mattress safe and clean.

question: Why do we always tell patients to finish their full course of antibiotics, even if they feel better?

options.A: It lowers the patient's blood pressure dangerously fast
options.B: It causes the drug to instantly accumulate in the liver
options.C: It immediately destroys all normal flora in the body
options.D: It leaves the strongest bacteria alive to cause stronger infections

explanation: Stopping early is a big no-no! It kills off the weak bacteria and leaves the tough ones behind to multiply and cause drug resistance.

question: What structure is compromised when a rectovaginal fistula forms?

options.A: The anovaginal septum
options.B: The inguinal ligament
options.C: The ureterovesical junction
options.D: The internal cervical os

explanation: The fistula forms when the partition or septum separating the rectum and vagina is damaged or breached. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h2)

question: Which of these is an example of an intrinsic (internal) risk factor for a patient?

options.A: An improperly calibrated infusion pump
options.B: Muscle weakness from advanced age
options.C: A wet floor in the hallway
options.D: Poor lighting in the patient room

explanation: Intrinsic risks come from inside the patient's own body, like age-related muscle weakness, rather than from things around the ward.

question: Why do we only use glutaraldehyde on medical equipment instead of human skin?

options.A: It turns the skin bright yellow for several weeks.
options.B: It is a high-level disinfectant that releases toxic fumes and irritates skin.
options.C: It instantly evaporates when it touches human skin.
options.D: It only works when it is mixed with hot boiling water.

explanation: That's right! Glutaraldehyde is extremely harsh and gives off strong fumes, so it belongs in soaking tanks for instruments, never on a patient's skin.

question: What is the actual impact of FGM on childbirth, contrary to traditional beliefs?

options.A: Delivery times become much shorter and completely painless
options.B: The procedure permanently cures all forms of primary infertility
options.C: Scar tissue obstructs labor and increases childbirth risks
options.D: Hormonal levels rise significantly to support healthy pregnancies

explanation: Spot on! Instead of helping, FGM creates tough scar tissue that causes serious complications during delivery.

question: How can you best support a newly diagnosed hearing-impaired patient who feels lonely and isolated?

options.A: Connecting the patient with local support groups and rehabilitation
options.B: Limiting family visits to reduce communication fatigue
options.C: Focusing solely on medical treatments without addressing feelings
options.D: Telling the patient to avoid all social gatherings permanently

explanation: Connecting them to support groups and rehab programs helps them realize they aren't alone and teaches them awesome new ways to communicate.

question: What is the main goal behind how an operating room is designed?

options.A: Minimizing infection risk and keeping patients safe
options.B: Allowing family members to watch procedures
options.C: Speeding up the recovery time after surgery
options.D: Reducing the cost of surgical instruments

explanation: Spot on! Everything in the operating room layout is carefully planned to keep the area sterile and protect our patients from infections. You've got this!

question: Which lifestyle habit helps improve blood vessel health for men dealing with sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Regular physical exercise and weight loss
options.B: Increasing daily caffeine consumption
options.C: Reducing total hours of sleep each night
options.D: Avoiding all forms of dietary carbohydrates

explanation: Spot on! Staying active and managing weight keeps the heart and blood vessels healthy, which directly boosts sexual function.

question: Why is it a bad idea to use young children as interpreters during home visits?

options.A: Children are always too expensive to hire for home health visits
options.B: It can lead to clinical translation errors and breach client privacy
options.C: State laws prohibit anyone under eighteen from entering a bedroom
options.D: Medical terminology is too simple for young minds to comprehend

explanation: Totally! Kids shouldn't carry the stress of medical details, and misinterpretations can lead to serious health mistakes. Always look for an adult translator.

question: What term describes the thickening of the skin caused by chronic scratching and rubbing?

options.A: Maceration
options.B: Excoriation
options.C: Lichenification
options.D: Desquamation

explanation: Lichenification refers to thickened, leathery skin markings that develop after a patient repeatedly scratches or rubs an itchy area over a long period. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h5)

question: How many blood vessels are normally inside a healthy human umbilical cord?

options.A: Two arteries and two veins
options.B: Two veins and one artery
options.C: Two arteries and one vein
options.D: One artery and one vein

explanation: Correct! A normal umbilical cord has three vessels: two umbilical arteries carrying waste away from the baby, and one umbilical vein bringing fresh oxygen and nutrients. Easy peasy!

question: What happens to the body's normal breakdown pathways during a severe drug overdose?

options.A: They become completely saturated
options.B: They speed up to eliminate the drug instantly
options.C: They convert the drug into harmless vitamins
options.D: They shut down permanently within seconds

explanation: Think of it like a traffic jam: there is simply too much drug for the body's processing enzymes to handle all at once, so the pathways get completely overwhelmed.

question: A patient recovering from defibulation surgery is in the ward. What is a key nursing priority?

options.A: Restricting fluid intake to keep the surgical site dry
options.B: Applying tight pressure dressings to keep edges closed
options.C: Providing meticulous wound care to prevent new adhesion formation
options.D: Encouraging immediate heavy exercise to build strength

explanation: That's correct! Freshly separated wound edges can easily stick back together, making careful hygiene and separation techniques key nursing duties. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why is a lumbar puncture very dangerous for a patient with a brain mass causing high pressure inside the skull?

options.A: It will stop the heart instantly
options.B: It leads to instant paralysis
options.C: It causes severe kidney failure
options.D: It can trigger brain herniation

explanation: Exactly. Releasing fluid when pressure is already high can push brain tissue downward. Safety first—always check for high intracranial pressure!

question: Which drug class must patients NEVER mix with erectile dysfunction medications like sildenafil?

options.A: Topical antibiotics
options.B: Organic nitrates
options.C: Oral multivitamins
options.D: Antihistamines

explanation: Safety first! Mixing ED meds with nitrates can cause a massive, dangerous crash in blood pressure. Never combine them!

question: A hospital kitchen is planning meals for patients who do not eat pork due to religious beliefs. What is guiding this menu choice?

options.A: Cultural and religious preferences
options.B: Kitchen equipment capacity
options.C: Immediate staff availability
options.D: Seasonal food availability

explanation: Respecting religious and cultural food laws is a vital part of caring for the whole patient.

question: What is the main goal of public health agencies, as opposed to a regular hospital ward?

options.A: Managing health at a population level
options.B: Training medical doctors exclusively
options.C: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: Providing surgical operations only

explanation: You've got this! While hospital wards focus on one sick patient at a time, public health agencies look at the big picture—keeping whole communities healthy and preventing disease.

question: Which organ in the body is the main target for both Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C?

options.A: The lungs
options.B: The pancreas
options.C: The kidneys
options.D: The liver

explanation: Spot on! Both hepatitis B and C viruses attack liver cells, causing inflammation and long-term damage if left untreated.

question: During embryonic development, which structures form the female reproductive tract, including the fallopian tubes?

options.A: Ovarian cords
options.B: Urogenital sinus
options.C: Müllerian ducts
options.D: Wolffian ducts

explanation: The Müllerian ducts are the embryonic building blocks for the female reproductive system. If they don't develop quite right, it can lead to tubal or uterine variations.

question: Why do bacterial toxins in the gut cause diarrhea?

options.A: They block the reabsorption of solid waste in the rectum
options.B: They stimulate excess fluid secretion into the bowel lumen
options.C: They cause permanent paralysis of the abdominal muscles
options.D: They completely stop the production of digestive enzymes

explanation: When toxins irritate your gut lining, it reacts by rushing a lot of water and salt out into your intestines, causing watery stool to flush the germs out.

question: Why would a doctor choose a nasal endoscope instead of a basic speculum exam?

options.A: To stop sudden nosebleeds in the front septum
options.B: To measure air pressure inside the cheek sinuses
options.C: To test the patient's sense of smell
options.D: To look deep inside the nasal passages and sinus openings

explanation: Nasal endoscopes use tiny cameras and lights to see past the front of the nose into deeper areas a regular speculum can't reach.

question: What kind of data do you mainly collect in qualitative research?

options.A: Words, text, and descriptions of human experiences
options.B: Statistical percentages of patient readmissions
options.C: Exact laboratory blood chemistry measurements
options.D: Precise numerical vital signs recorded hourly

explanation: While quantitative loves numbers, qualitative loves words! It looks at interview notes and stories to understand human experiences.

question: Why is taking ART medications every single day so important for patients?

options.A: Missing a single dose causes immediate death from opportunistic infections.
options.B: Inconsistent taking of drugs can cause the virus to mutate and develop resistance to treatment.
options.C: Taking pills at irregular times makes the medication taste much worse.
options.D: Strict adherence is only necessary during the first month of therapy.

explanation: Consistency is key! If a patient skips doses, drug levels drop in the blood, giving the crafty virus a chance to change its form and beat the medicine.

question: What position should the nurse place the patient in before starting a nebulizer treatment?

options.A: Flat on their back with no pillows
options.B: Toned flat on their stomach
options.C: Lying strictly on their left side
options.D: Upright sitting or semi-Fowler's position

explanation: Sitting upright lets the chest expand fully, helping the medication travel deep into the lower airways. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h5)

question: A patient with type 2 diabetes needs help managing their meals. What is a great, simple tip to share first?

options.A: Replace all water intake with fresh vegetable juices only
options.B: Cook your vegetables without any seasoning or oil whatsoever
options.C: Stop eating all forms of food for two days of the week
options.D: Fill half of your meal plate with non-starchy, colorful vegetables

explanation: You nailed it! The plate method is a fantastic, visual way to help patients control portions and get enough fiber without stressful calorie counting.

question: What is the 'harm reduction myth' regarding medicalised FGM?

options.A: The idea that cutting less tissue prevents all future pain
options.B: The assumption that older girls heal faster than babies
options.C: The belief that clinical FGM is safer and causes fewer complications
options.D: The theory that local herbs stop infections better than antibiotics

explanation: Some health workers wrongly believe that sterile tools make the procedure safe, ignoring the lasting harm. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why do anticholinergic drugs often cause annoying side effects like dry mouth and blurred vision?

options.A: They block parasympathetic nerve signals throughout the whole body
options.B: They cause a sudden drop in the patient's blood pressure
options.C: They irritate the mucous membranes in the head and neck
options.D: They dehydrate the patient by increasing kidney urine output

explanation: Because these signals help control our body's moisture and secretions, blocking them dries things up everywhere—leading to dry mouth and blurry eyes.

question: Why is it important to know the difference between a mechanical soft and a pureed diet?

options.A: To ensure the kitchen staff uses less cooking oil
options.B: To prevent giving unsafe food textures to a patient at risk of choking
options.C: To calculate the exact financial cost of hospital meals
options.D: To determine when the patient can stop taking oral medications

explanation: Giving a solid piece of food to someone who requires a pureed diet can lead to airway obstruction and aspiration pneumonia. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h3)

question: What does the letter 'P' stand for in the PDSA cycle used for quality improvement?

options.A: Punish
options.B: Protocol
options.C: Plan
options.D: Patient

explanation: In the PDSA cycle, Plan refers to identifying the problem and planning a small change to test. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h6)

question: What do we call the emotional exhaustion and loss of care caused by long-term stress at work?

options.A: Hypothermia
options.B: Hysteria
options.C: Burnout
options.D: Hyperglycemia

explanation: Burnout is real in demanding fields like nursing. It's that feeling of complete mental and emotional tiredness from too much stress. Take care of your mental health!

question: How does pursed-lip breathing help someone struggling with chronic breathing problems?

options.A: It increases the heart rate to improve tissue perfusion.
options.B: It stops mucus production in the large bronchi.
options.C: It creates back-pressure that keeps small airways from collapsing when they breathe out.
options.D: It forces all carbon dioxide out of the stomach immediately.

explanation: Breathing out through pursed lips acts like a brake, keeping airways open longer so the lungs can empty out more old air.

question: Why is family planning so important for mothers' health in Nigeria?

options.A: It helps reduce maternal mortality by allowing proper pregnancy spacing.
options.B: It removes the need for routine antenatal care visits.
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of chronic illnesses.
options.D: It guarantees financial stability for large households.

explanation: Spot on! Giving the body enough time to recover between pregnancies protects the mother's health and greatly lowers the risk of complications during childbirth.

question: What is the main job of thiamine (Vitamin B1) in our cells?

options.A: It wraps around nerves to speed up signals
options.B: It helps brain cells turn glucose into energy
options.C: It stops white blood cells from overreacting
options.D: It carries oxygen through the bloodstream

explanation: That's right! Thiamine acts like fuel for the brain, helping cells process glucose so they can stay alive and active.

question: What is the primary role of the nurse while the physician performs the lumbar puncture?

options.A: Administer oxygen through a nasal cannula to all patients
options.B: Help the patient maintain the curled position and offer reassurance
options.C: Monitor the patient's heart rhythm using a 12-lead ECG machine
options.D: Hold the collection tubes and write laboratory labels later

explanation: You got it! Staying still is crucial, so holding the patient steady and offering calming words are key nursing duties.

question: A patient eats a very salty meal. What is their body most likely to do right after?

options.A: Extracellular fluid shifts completely inside the cells
options.B: Thirst increases and the kidneys retain more water
options.C: The kidneys immediately excrete all circulating sodium
options.D: Blood pressure drops rapidly due to sudden dehydration

explanation: Exactly! High salt makes you thirsty and tells your kidneys to hold onto water to keep everything nicely diluted.

question: What is the primary physiological problem in all forms of distributive shock?

options.A: Massive dilation of blood vessels creating relative hypovolemia
options.B: Complete physical blockage of blood flowing into the heart
options.C: Sudden destruction of red blood cells by the immune system
options.D: Primary failure of kidney function leading to severe fluid retention

explanation: Distributive shock is characterized by abnormal widening of blood vessels, making the normal volume of blood insufficient to fill the vascular space. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h5)

question: What should you do first if you spot an unexplained, non-healing sore on a patient's tongue?

options.A: Scrape the surface firmly to see if it bleeds like thrush
options.B: Prescribe an antibacterial mouthwash for two weeks
options.C: Document its exact size, shape, and refer for medical evaluation
options.D: Advise the patient to stop using commercial toothpaste

explanation: Always record clear details of the lesion and send the patient for a proper medical review to rule out anything serious.

question: Why are cooking demonstrations more effective than simply handing out printed pamphlets?

options.A: They show mothers how to use local foods in practical, hands-on ways
options.B: They eliminate the need for any further nursing follow-up
options.C: They prove that imported foods are always superior
options.D: They take less time than talking to individuals

explanation: Hands-on cooking demos help learners visualize and practice preparing nutritious meals with ingredients they already own. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h6)

question: When you tell a patient the 'indication' of a drug, what are you actually explaining to them?

options.A: To help the nurse calculate the correct financial cost of the prescription
options.B: To teach the patient the chemical formula of the active ingredient
options.C: To determine how quickly the drug will be eliminated by the kidneys
options.D: To ensure the patient knows the therapeutic purpose of the treatment

explanation: An 'indication' just means the reason for taking the drug—what illness or symptom it is meant to fix. Simple as that!

question: As a nurse, what major emotional or psychological challenge should you anticipate for a patient facing a radical hysterectomy?

options.A: Complete loss of long-term memory function
options.B: Sudden denial of the physical diagnosis by family members
options.C: Intense fear of hospital food and environmental sounds
options.D: Body image disturbance and grief over lost fertility

explanation: Spot on. Losing reproductive organs can trigger profound emotional grief regarding womanhood, body image, and the ability to have children. Compassionate nursing support is everything here.

question: Why is it important for a school counseling service to be confidential?

options.A: It guarantees that parents will never be informed of any school issues
options.B: It encourages students to seek help without fear of stigma or punishment
options.C: It allows the school to hide student disciplinary records from the public
options.D: It replaces the need for academic tutoring in difficult subjects

explanation: Well done! Confidentiality creates trust, making students feel safe enough to share their worries without fear of being judged.

question: Why is getting a detailed witness account so important when assessing a patient with a suspected paroxysmal disorder?

options.A: Witnesses can accurately measure the exact brain wave frequency.
options.B: Doctors rely on family members to prescribe the correct medication.
options.C: Patients often have no memory of the actual event.
options.D: Patients always exaggerate their physical symptoms during attacks.

explanation: Because altered awareness or unconsciousness is common during seizures, bystanders provide the most reliable description of what happened. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h5)

question: What type of tissue does a somatic reflex target?

options.A: Smooth muscle of blood vessels
options.B: Cardiac muscle
options.C: Endocrine glands
options.D: Skeletal muscle

explanation: Somatic reflexes deal with your voluntary skeletal muscles—the ones that let you move your arms, legs, and body around.

question: How do home care nurses help prevent clients from ending up back in the hospital?

options.A: By prescribing stronger emergency medications independently
options.B: By catching subtle signs of clinical deterioration early
options.C: By banning the client from visiting local hospitals
options.D: By admitting the client to a nursing home immediately

explanation: Brilliant! By keeping a close eye on small changes, we can catch problems early before they turn into major emergencies.

question: How does the cerebellum use an 'efference copy' during a voluntary movement?

options.A: To produce neurotransmitters required for neuromuscular transmission
options.B: To directly contract skeletal muscles without involving the cortex
options.C: To store long-term procedural memories of past movements
options.D: To compare intended motor commands with actual sensory feedback

explanation: An efference copy is like a duplicate draft of the brain's movement plan sent to the cerebellum so it can check: 'Did our body actually do what we wanted it to do?' Brilliant nursing brain at work!

question: A postoperative patient refuses to eat because food always brings severe belly pain and nausea. What is your best nursing action?

options.A: Administer prescribed pain and anti-nausea medications thirty minutes before the next meal
options.B: Remove all food trays permanently and start total parenteral nutrition
options.C: Force the patient to finish the entire meal tray immediately
options.D: Tell the patient that eating is mandatory for legal discharge

explanation: Brilliant! Managing pain and nausea before mealtime makes eating comfortable so the patient can actually get their nutrition.

question: Why is it important for a nurse to understand a patient's living situation and financial stability?

options.A: They determine the exact surgical approach needed for recovery
options.B: They replace the need to conduct a review of body systems
options.C: Insurances require this data to calculate daily calorie counts
options.D: These factors directly affect the ability to follow medical treatments

explanation: Spot on! If money is tight or housing is unstable, buying prescriptions or returning for follow-ups can be a massive hurdle.

question: What is the main purpose of a health screening test?

options.A: To replace a clinical doctor's formal diagnosis
options.B: To cure an advanced chronic illness permanently
options.C: To prevent the initial exposure to a pathogen
options.D: To find hidden disease before symptoms appear

explanation: Screening is designed to catch health problems early in people who feel well so that prompt treatment can begin. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h3)

question: What major event marks the exact beginning of the third stage of labour?

options.A: Complete dilation of the cervix
options.B: Delivery of the infant
options.C: Expulsion of the mucous plug
options.D: Rupture of the amniotic membranes

explanation: Great thinking! The moment the baby is safely out, the third stage kicks off—and it wraps up once the placenta is delivered too.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical problem caused by untreated anosmia?

options.A: Danger of failing to detect smoke or gas leaks
options.B: Inability to hear high-pitched vocal tones
options.C: Decreased appetite and unintended weight loss
options.D: Distorted enjoyment of food due to lost flavor

explanation: You got it! Hearing is handled by auditory pathways in the temporal lobe, not the nose. Smell loss won't affect how well you hear high notes.

question: Why should a DRF pricing strategy include an inflation buffer?

options.A: To discourage patients from buying unnecessary medications
options.B: To pay for the transport costs of delivering emergency care
options.C: To generate bonus income for the hospital management board
options.D: To ensure future re-stocking can cover rising market prices

explanation: You've got it! Prices in the market go up. Adding a small inflation buffer ensures that when you need to buy a new batch of drugs, you'll actually have enough money to afford them.

question: What is the medical term for blood collecting inside the pleural space?

options.A: Pleural effusion
options.B: Hemothorax
options.C: Chylothorax
options.D: Pneumothorax

explanation: You've got this! 'Hemo' means blood and 'thorax' means chest, so blood in the chest is a hemothorax.

question: Which factor strongly contributes to cholera outbreaks during the rainy season in our communities?

options.A: Lower ambient temperatures at night
options.B: Dry winds blowing dust into houses
options.C: Contamination of drinking water sources
options.D: Increased population migration to cities

explanation: Spot on! Heavy rains easily wash surface waste into local water sources, which is how waterborne infections like cholera spread so quickly.

question: What does the word 'vesicant' mean when talking about certain chemo drugs?

options.A: Natural supplements that cure nausea caused by treatment
options.B: Solutions used to clean the skin before a surgical incision
options.C: Drugs that cause severe tissue damage if they leak outside the vein
options.D: Medications that are only given orally in pill form

explanation: Vesicants are tricky drugs! If they escape the vein into the skin, they can cause blistering and tissue damage, which is why nurses watch IV sites so closely.

question: What is the primary function of the epiglottis during swallowing?

options.A: Filter bacteria out of incoming swallowed liquids
options.B: Produce saliva to break down solid food particles
options.C: Pump air directly into the upper respiratory tract
options.D: Cover the larynx to direct food into the esophagus

explanation: The epiglottis acts as a protective lid that folds over the windpipe when we swallow, keeping food out of the airway. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T7#GNS324_U6_T7_h1)

question: Why should a nurse apply gentle pressure to the nasolacrimal duct after giving eye drops?

options.A: To help spread the liquid evenly across the eyeball surface
options.B: To stop the patient from blinking too rapidly
options.C: To seal the eyelids shut until the medication dries completely
options.D: To keep the medication from draining into the nasal passage and causing systemic effects

explanation: Blocking the tear duct stops the medicine from entering the nose and bloodstream, keeping its action localized to the eye. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h5)

question: A patient with Pick's disease tries to wander out of the ward wearing only a hospital gown. What is your best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Apply soft wrist restraints immediately to prevent wandering attempts.
options.B: Gently redirect the patient toward a quiet lounge area with a familiar activity.
options.C: Explain firmly and logically why leaving the ward is dangerous for health.
options.D: Lock the patient inside the hospital room until visiting hours are over.

explanation: Redirection is your best friend here! Arguing or reasoning usually fails because of brain damage, but gently steering them to a cozy spot keeps them safe without a fight.

question: What is the main purpose of emergency obstetric care networks?

options.A: To replace the need for routine antenatal checkups
options.B: To reduce the overall birth rate in rural populations
options.C: To provide long-term family planning counseling
options.D: To treat sudden, life-threatening complications during birth

explanation: Correct! These networks ensure that when a sudden crisis hits during labor, mothers can get life-saving emergency care fast.

question: Which muscular structure separates the chest (thoracic) cavity from the belly (abdominopelvic) cavity?

options.A: Peritoneum
options.B: Mediastinum
options.C: Pleura
options.D: Diaphragm

explanation: The diaphragm is a dome-shaped breathing muscle that forms a neat floor for the chest and a roof for the belly.

question: What is a frequent cause of a false-positive Mantoux test in individuals from other countries?

options.A: Prior vaccination with the BCG vaccine
options.B: Having a severe viral cold during testing
options.C: Receiving the injection too deep in the skin
options.D: Taking daily multi-vitamin supplements

explanation: The BCG vaccine, given in many countries to prevent childhood TB, can cause the immune system to react to PPD, creating a false-positive skin test. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h7)

question: How do nurses properly check for pitting oedema at the bedside?

options.A: Measuring the circumference of the limb with a flexible tape measure
options.B: Squeezing the muscle belly firmly to test for deep pain reflexes
options.C: Pressing a finger firmly against the swollen skin over a bony area for a few seconds
options.D: Applying a cold pack to see how fast the skin temperature drops

explanation: You got it! Pressing firmly over a bone (like the shin) pushes the fluid aside momentarily. If an indent stays behind, that's a positive 'pit'!

question: Which of the following is NOT a common reason why infections cause nutrient depletion?

options.A: Increased physical exercise and weightlifting routines
options.B: Higher metabolic demands caused by persistent fever
options.C: Loss of appetite and reduced food consumption
options.D: Nutrient loss through vomiting and severe diarrhea

explanation: Sick patients with infections do not typically engage in heavy exercise; rather, fever, poor appetite, and GI losses drive their nutrient depletion. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h5)

question: How does male andropause usually differ from female menopause?

options.A: It involves a slow and gradual decline in hormone levels
options.B: It causes an immediate and complete stop to all sperm production
options.C: It affects every single man at exactly age fifty years
options.D: It occurs during early adolescence rather than late adulthood

explanation: Correct! Unlike the quicker hormone drop in female menopause, men experience a very gradual, slow decrease in hormone levels as they age.

question: A patient is prescribed liquid iron. What should the nurse teach them to prevent stained teeth?

options.A: Dilute the medication in warm milk before swallowing
options.B: Drink the liquid through a straw and brush teeth after
options.C: Rinse the mouth with strong hydrogen peroxide afterward
options.D: Swallow the liquid quickly without letting it touch the lips

explanation: Liquid iron loves to stain teeth enamel! Using a straw helps bypass the teeth entirely, keeping that bright smile safe.

question: Which of these is NOT used to measure the quality of a nursing unit?

options.A: Patient fall rates and hospital-acquired infections
options.B: Medication error tracking and incident reports
options.C: Patient satisfaction survey scores
options.D: The favorite holiday destination of the nursing staff

explanation: You nailed it! Quality care is measured by safety outcomes and patient happiness, not personal staff trivia.

question: What is a major challenge facing families who seek formal custodial care in urban Nigerian cities?

options.A: High out-of-pocket costs because insurance rarely covers non-medical care
options.B: Strict government laws that forbid hiring private home caregivers
options.C: Complete lack of any individuals willing to work as caregivers
options.D: An overabundance of free public nursing homes in every neighborhood

explanation: Because health insurance typically covers acute medical care rather than long-term custodial help, families must pay out of pocket for private aides. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h6)

question: Which heart sign usually appears late in severe, untreated asphyxia?

options.A: Bounding hypertension
options.B: Severe bradycardia
options.C: Rapid atrial flutter
options.D: Normal sinus rhythm

explanation: At first, the heart pumps faster to cope with the stress. But as the lack of oxygen drags on, the heart muscle gets tired and weak, causing the heart rate to drop dangerously low (bradycardia).

question: Your patient has chest congestion with thick mucus that just won't budge. What drug class should you expect the doctor to order?

options.A: A topical anesthetic
options.B: An opioid suppressant
options.C: An expectorant
options.D: A loop diuretic

explanation: You nailed it. Thick, immobile chest congestion is the number one reason to prescribe an expectorant.

question: What is the primary function of the fimbriae on the fallopian tubes?

options.A: To secrete hormones that stop ovulation
options.B: To block sperm from entering the abdominal cavity
options.C: To catch the released egg from the ovary
options.D: To produce mucus for lubrication during intercourse

explanation: These finger-like projections sweep over the ovary surface to guide the newly released egg into the tube. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary cause of a vasovagal reaction during cervical manipulation or MVA?

options.A: An acute drop in the patient's body temperature
options.B: Complete blockage of the airway by mucus
options.C: Sudden stimulation of nerves around the cervix
options.D: A severe allergic reaction to the plastic syringe

explanation: Stretching or manipulating the cervix triggers nerve responses that can lower the heart rate and blood pressure, causing fainting or dizziness. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h7)

question: How is pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) affecting the Fallopian tubes primarily treated in a stable patient?

options.A: Continuous peritoneal dialysis
options.B: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Immediate emergency surgery
options.D: Radiation therapy

explanation: You're crushing it. Because PID is an infection, the frontline treatment is medical—hitting it hard with the right antibiotics to clear the bacteria.

question: As a safe nursing habit, why should an arterial line insertion site always be left uncovered by heavy bed linens?

options.A: To allow immediate visual detection of bleeding or disconnection
options.B: To ensure the patient can easily remove the sterile dressing themselves
options.C: To let air circulate so the skin around the puncture site stays dry
options.D: To prevent the electronic blood pressure monitor from overheating

explanation: Safety first! Because arterial pressure is so high, if a line slips out under heavy blankets, a patient could lose a dangerous amount of blood before anyone notices.

question: Why must we encourage patients to drink plenty of water right after a barium meal?

options.A: To prevent the patient from developing a high fever
options.B: To prevent severe constipation caused by the barium
options.C: To dissolve any leftover barium remaining in the stomach
options.D: To speed up the absorption of the contrast into the blood

explanation: Spot on! Barium soaks up water like a sponge as it moves down, so extra fluids save your patient from a hard, painful time in the toilet. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h6)

question: Why can repeated or chronic ovarian infections lead to long-term fertility problems?

options.A: White blood cells destroy all female hormones
options.B: The uterus shrinks to prevent egg implantation
options.C: Scar tissue develops during healing, blocking pelvic structures
options.D: The ovaries permanently stop making estrogen

explanation: Just like a skin wound leaves a scar, healing reproductive tissue can form adhesions and scar tissue that block the tubes and trap the ovaries, making pregnancy difficult.

question: Why must a nurse position a patient upright before giving oral medications?

options.A: It speeds up the first-pass metabolism in the liver
options.B: It allows the nurse to check the pulse more easily
options.C: Gravity helps the medication go down safely and prevents choking
options.D: It stops the stomach acid from rising into the throat

explanation: Sitting at a 90-degree angle uses gravity to guide the pill into the esophagus and protects the airway from accidental aspiration. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h2)

question: Who primarily handled the care of sick family members in most ancient households?

options.A: Professional monastic orders
options.B: Government-certified physicians
options.C: Women within the home
options.D: Trained military nurses

explanation: Before formal institutions, caring for the sick was mainly a domestic duty performed by female family members. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h1)

question: Where is the best place on an infant's body to give an intramuscular (IM) vaccine?

options.A: Abdominal subcutaneous tissue
options.B: Deltoid muscle in the upper arm
options.C: Gluteus maximus muscle in the buttocks
options.D: Vastus lateralis muscle in the thigh

explanation: Correct! The thigh muscle is plump and safe in babies, helping us avoid the sciatic nerve in the buttocks.

question: A patient says, 'My cough is gone after a month, so I want to stop my TB pills.' What is your best response as a nurse?

options.A: Take only the rifampicin and throw away the other pills since they cause too many side effects
options.B: Stop the drugs immediately since the absence of a cough proves the lungs are fully healed
options.C: Switch to half the dose for the remaining months to save money on prescription refills
options.D: Continue taking all pills for the full months prescribed to kill hidden germs and prevent resistance

explanation: Feeling better doesn't mean the germs are gone! Patients must finish their full course to wipe out hidden bacteria and avoid resistance.

question: A village starts the year with no cholera, but 10 people fall sick by March. What do these 10 new cases represent?

options.A: The recovery rate of the infected population
options.B: The prevalence of cholera in the village
options.C: The mortality rate of the disease outbreak
options.D: The incidence of cholera for that period

explanation: Because these 10 folks developed the illness during that time window, they are the brand-new cases—making it the incidence!

question: What are the two main synthetic hormones used in most hormonal birth control methods?

options.A: Thyroxine and calcitonin
options.B: Estrogen and progestin
options.C: Cortisol and aldosterone
options.D: Insulin and glucagon

explanation: Great start! Hormonal contraceptives work by mimicking natural female hormones using synthetic forms of estrogen and progestin to keep the cycle regulated and prevent pregnancy.

question: How does gender expression differ from gender identity?

options.A: Gender expression is how a person shows their gender to the outside world
options.B: Gender expression is strictly determined by chromosomes at birth
options.C: Gender expression is purely biological and never changes over time
options.D: Gender expression only refers to a person's internal psychological thoughts

explanation: While identity is internal, expression is external and includes outward signs like clothing, behavior, and mannerisms that communicate gender to others. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h1)

question: A patient comes in with a suspected blood clot in their leg vein (deep vein thrombosis). What scan will the doctor likely order?

options.A: Renal B-Mode ultrasound
options.B: Pelvic M-Mode ultrasound
options.C: Cardiac echocardiogram
options.D: Vascular Doppler ultrasound

explanation: A vascular Doppler scan is specifically designed to peek inside blood vessels and catch clots early.

question: A patient looks pale and feels dizzy halfway through a large fluid drain. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Push the drainage catheter further into the skin
options.B: Inform the doctor and monitor vital signs closely
options.C: Leave the room to document the procedure chart
options.D: Encourage the patient to drink a glass of water

explanation: Dizziness and paleness mean the blood pressure might be dropping. Alerting the team and checking vitals keeps the patient safe.

question: What is the biggest risk of reusing disposable syringes in a clinic?

options.A: Transmission of blood-borne infections
options.B: Severe allergic reactions to leftover air
options.C: Permanent numbing of the injection site
options.D: Immediate breakdown of the plastic barrel

explanation: You've got this! Reusing syringes transfers tiny traces of blood and germs from person to person, spreading serious viruses like HIV and hepatitis. Always use a fresh syringe!

question: Why is establishing a baseline neurological assessment important for a patient?

options.A: It eliminates the need for vital sign monitoring
options.B: It gives a starting point to track future changes in status
options.C: It completely prevents any future neurological complications
options.D: It determines the patient's exact date of hospital discharge

explanation: Having a clear baseline allows the healthcare team to notice early signs of improvement or deterioration. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h1)

question: What two structures combine to form the striatum?

options.A: Caudate nucleus and putamen
options.B: Putamen and globus pallidus
options.C: Caudate nucleus and substantia nigra
options.D: Thalamus and subthalamic nucleus

explanation: The caudate nucleus and the putamen together make up the striatum, which is the main receiving area for inputs coming into the basal ganglia from the cerebral cortex. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T12#GNS211_U3_T12_h1)

question: How does Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) differ from basic health education?

options.A: BCC focuses on active behavior change rather than just sharing information
options.B: Basic health education involves no communication at all
options.C: BCC is only used inside tertiary hospitals by doctors
options.D: Basic education is meant for children while BCC is for adults

explanation: Think of it this way: health education gives people the facts, but BCC goes a step further to help them actually overcome personal and social barriers to take action. You're building solid community nursing foundations!

question: When is a nurse researcher most likely to choose a quasi-experimental design instead of a true experiment?

options.A: When the nurse wants to avoid doing any data analysis
options.B: When all patients must receive the exact same treatment
options.C: When random assignment of patients is impossible or unethical
options.D: When there is no budget to buy any research equipment

explanation: Clinical realities often prevent random assignment, such as studying existing groups like patients on two different hospital floors, forcing researchers to use quasi-methods. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h3)

question: What is the main reason a hospital or workplace sets up an organisational structure?

options.A: To monitor daily patient vital sign records
options.B: To calculate monthly staff salaries and bonuses
options.C: To outline reporting lines and divide job tasks
options.D: To design marketing strategies for new products

explanation: Think of an organisational structure like a hospital blueprint! It helps everyone know who reports to who, and who handles specific tasks so work runs smoothly.

question: What is the main goal of palliative care?

options.A: To shorten the dying process
options.B: To replace family caregiving
options.C: To cure terminal illnesses
options.D: To improve quality of life

explanation: Palliative care focuses primarily on relieving symptoms and stress to give the patient and family the best possible quality of life. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T11#GNS321_U4_T11_h1)

question: What is a frequent, painful problem caused by excessive pushing during bowel movements in pregnancy?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Placental abruption
options.C: Preeclampsia
options.D: Hemorrhoids

explanation: You got it! Straining puts heavy pressure on the pelvic veins, which often leads to swollen, painful hemorrhoids (piles).

question: Why are community nurses and midwives often called the 'gatekeepers' of the referral process?

options.A: They approve the financial budget for community health centers
options.B: They are the first to spot complications and decide when to escalate care
options.C: They decide which patients are wealthy enough to afford hospital care
options.D: They physically transport every single patient to the general hospital

explanation: Spotting trouble early is your superpower as a nurse! Because you monitor mums and babies closely, you make that vital first call to transfer them when things go south.
